note: Fails if a blocking finding stops being an `error` at its located path, or if validate stops reporting every one at once in source order: `table_is_register` (`demo/nam` names a register with tables `a` and `b`), `variable_not_in_table` (`annan` has segments only in `nam/b`), `outside_availability` (`imp` starts in 2018), `ambiguous_window` (two variables claim `Del` in `amb` over 2019), `preliminary_without_edition` (`pre`'s `Mat` for 2020 comes only from a preliminary release), `edition_not_found` (`imp` has final releases only), `period_default_on_dated_table`, `period_on_timeless_table` (`tid` has no dated occurrence, so it is timeless) and `period_not_orderable` (a scalar `{from: 2020, to: 2019}`). Each source binds one variable that raises nothing else, except where noted. Four more sources pin the window and edition edges: `final` does not lift `preliminary_without_edition` (`edt`'s `V` for 2020 is only in a preliminary release beside an unstated primary); two forms of `V` inside the one selected preliminary release for 2018 (`V` int, `W` decimal, both shadowed) are an `ambiguous_window`, not a silent first-wins entry (with the release's F7 `edition_disagreement` warning); `bara`, only in `suc/gammal` (2017), requested for 2019 when `suc/ny` serves, is `outside_availability`, not `variable_not_in_table`; and `edition_not_found` is per period item (`[2019, 2020]` with a preliminary release only in 2020 fails 2019). Three sources pin the stored preliminary selection, the segments the builder builds by its own rules from the preliminary releases' used and shadowed occurrences alone: a rival claim (`edt`'s preliminary 2021 release documents `V` under a second key) is an `ambiguous_window`, not a silent clear window (and because the selection merges 2020 and 2021 into one run before the rival pass, as the primary segments do, `edition-item` gets an `ambiguous_window` over 2020 after its `edition_not_found`); forms across selected releases (the preliminary 2022H1 release types `V` decimal, the preliminary 2022 one int) are one component of whole overlapping occurrences, so all of 2022 is an `ambiguous_window`, not a first-wins pick, and one segment gives no `form_change` (with H1's F7 `edition_disagreement`); and the selection compares reg-core's `Form`, label included: the preliminary 2024H1 release labels `V` `Antal`, the preliminary 2024 one `Värde`, same spelling and type, so all of 2024 is an `ambiguous_window`, not a clear window.
